title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. In this 'quatrième mouture' of Analysis situs, Grothendieck works with an abstract 'magasin' (store) M = (M, ≤, ≪, |·|). Its elements are 'pieces', thought of as tame cells or compact pieces of a space. The relations are: ≤ (containment); ≪ (a strong, interior-type containment); |·| (a dimension- or support-type invariant); ⋔ / ≉ (compatibility of two pieces); and |o| ('disposition externe': two pieces lie outside each other, essentially with disjoint interiors). The previous page introduced 'polyhedral' variants. One is ≪_pol. The other is ⋔_pol: X ⋔_pol Y means X and Y are compatible and, for all X' ≤ X and Y' ≤ Y, the down-set X̃'∩Ỹ' is empty or has a largest element. That is, the meet of two subcells is again a single cell. Figpol(M) ⊂ Fig(M) was defined there as the figures whose pieces are pairwise ⋔_pol.

This page. It first unwinds the definition of Figpol(M): the subsets F ⊂ M such that
(a) F is closed downward for ≤;
(b) any X, Y in F are polyhedrally compatible. Condition (b) has two parts:
- 1°: pieces of X not in the common part and pieces of Y not in the common part are in external disposition, X' |o| Y'. That is, X and Y meet only along common faces.
- 2°: for all X' ≤ X and Y' ≤ Y, X̃'∩Ỹ' is empty or has a largest element. This is the 'intersection property': two faces meet in a single face or not at all.
In modern terms a polyhedral figure is (the face poset of) a cell complex in which every pairwise intersection of closed cells is a closed cell or empty. This is the polyhedral-complex / meet-semilattice condition, as opposed to the weaker regular-CW condition.

NB. Even when M is 'polyidéal' (≪ = ≪_pol), the inclusion Figpol(M) ⊊ Fig(M) is in general strict. The example is a circle made of two arcs glued at both endpoints. The two arcs meet in two points, so the intersection of their down-sets has no largest element: this is a figure but not a polyhedral one. Marginal sketches of triangles with an inscribed arc illustrate pieces with X ≪ Y but not X ≪_pol Y.

Scholie. The algebraic properties of 𝓕 = Figpol(M), with ≤, ≪_pol, ⋔_pol and its relations to M, are 'essentially the same' as those of Fig(M) with ≤, ≪, ⋔. The only difference is how ⋔_pol is spelled out in terms of |o|.

Proposition. For F, G in Figpol the following are equivalent:
(i) {F, G} is bounded above;
(ii) the supremum Sup(F, G) exists;
(iii) F ∪ G is in Figpol(M);
(iv) X ⋔_pol Y for all X in F and Y in G.
One then writes F ⋔_pol G. This is the consistency or coherence property: pairwise-compatible pieces glue, and the join of two bounded figures is their union.

Convention: the index 'pol' will be dropped when the context is polyhedral. The page ends by announcing 'atlas polyédral'. This is defined on the next page, like an ordinary ('spacieux') atlas but using Figpol, with axioms Magat pol a–c'.

Purpose. The page is part of an axiomatic, poset-theoretic foundation for tame topology (the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse). It separates a 'spacious' theory, convenient for figures as general as possible, from a 'polyhedral' theory, convenient for standard decompositions into pieces.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The proposition is plausible: (iii)⇒(ii)⇒(i) is formal. (iv)⇒(iii) needs only downward closure plus pairwise compatibility. (i)⇒(iv) holds because any upper bound H in Figpol contains F ∪ G, and pieces of H are pairwise ⋔_pol.

Minor gap: the proof of the proposition is not given, and the scholie's claim that 'the formal properties are essentially the same' is asserted, not checked ('On devrait prendre en revue les propositions pertinentes...').

The two-arc circle is a figure but not polyhedral only if the arcs are taken as pieces of M. Subdividing (three arcs) would give a polyhedral figure of the same underlying set. So the strictness concerns figures as decomposed objects, not their underlying sets. Grothendieck does not make this explicit here.

ideas.what: Polyhedral compatibility ⋔_pol: two pieces meet only along common faces (external disposition |o| off the common part), and any two subfaces meet in a single face or not at all.
ideas.modern_name: Intersection property of polyhedral / simplicial complexes; face poset is a meet-semilattice (vs. regular CW complex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology (Alexander, Whitehead); poset form via CW-posets (Björner 1984)
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished 1986 Analysis situs notes; the Esquisse d'un programme only calls for a 'topologie modérée' without this axiomatics

ideas.what: Figpol(M) ⊊ Fig(M) even for polyidéal M, with the circle formed by two arcs as counterexample.
ideas.modern_name: Regular CW / Δ-complex structures that are not polyhedral (two-cell circle)

ideas.what: Proposition: for polyhedral figures, being bounded above, having a supremum, having a polyhedral union, and pairwise compatibility of their pieces are all equivalent.
ideas.modern_name: Coherence (bounded-complete / pairwise-consistency) property, as in coherence spaces and Scott domains; gluing of subcomplexes

ideas.what: Methodological scholie: 'spacious' relations (≪, ⋔) versus 'polyhedral' relations (≪_pol, ⋔_pol) give parallel formal theories, differing only in how compatibility is expressed via external disposition |o|.
ideas.modern_name: Parallel between o-minimal/tame cell decompositions and PL/polyhedral structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (o-minimal triangulation), Shiota (PL tame topology)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a purely order-theoretic axiomatics ('magasin', figures, atlases) in which polyhedral structures form a sub-theory of a more general 'spacious' tame topology. He asserts the formal properties transfer but leaves the review of the relevant propositions undone. This axiomatic poset-theoretic tame topology was not developed in the later literature, which went via o-minimality instead.
missed.quote: On devrait prendre en revue les propositions pertinentes... Je signale seulement celle-ci
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A combinatorial or order-theoretic foundation for tame topology, comparing CW-poset or polyhedral face-poset axioms with abstract 'compact piece' structures, could connect o-minimal triangulation theory, face posets (Björner) and pointless/locale-style approaches. No one seems to have formalised Grothendieck's magasin framework.

missed.claim: The proposition 'bounded ⇔ sup exists ⇔ union is a figure ⇔ pairwise compatibility' makes Figpol(M) a coherent, pairwise-consistent domain of finite subcomplexes. This is an implicit link between Grothendieck's tame-topology project and the coherence-space / Scott-domain structures of logic and semantics.
missed.quote: (i) {F,G} majoré par ≤ (ii) Sup≤(F,G) existe (iii) F∪G ... ∈ Figpol(M) (iv) ∀X∈F̃,Y∈G̃, on a X ⋔pol Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly a curiosity. It suggests that the poset of polyhedral figures could be studied with domain-theoretic tools, but the content itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary: an intersection property for polyhedral complexes, a two-arc circle counterexample, and a routine gluing proposition. The interest is historical, as part of Grothendieck's unpublished abstract axiomatics of tame topology ('magasins', polyhedral atlases), whose existence and detail are not in the published record.
transcription_corrections: Condition 1° most likely reads '∀X' ∈ X̃ ∖ X̃∩Ỹ, Y' ∈ Ỹ ∖ X̃∩Ỹ ⟹ X' |o| Y'' (set differences), not 'X̃∩X̌∩Ỹ'.
Condition 2° should read '∀X'∈X̃, Y'∈Ỹ, X̃'∩Ỹ' est vide ou a un plus grand élément' (primes on the intersected down-sets), consistent with the definition on p.17.
NB line: rather 'Même si M est polyidéal — on a en général une inclusion stricte Figpol(M) ⊊ Fig(M)'. 'polyédral — ainsi on a toujours' looks like a misreading.
The cell 'pour M [?] origine polyédral convenable' is likely 'pour M (magasin d'un) modèle polyédral convenable' or similar.
The final heading should be 'Atlas polyédral' (cf. next page 'atlas polyédral'), not 'Atelier polyédral'.

Margin by the triangle sketches: 'Exemples de figures avec X ≪ Y mais non X ≪pol Y (1 indicateur des 2 [?])'. The sketch label reads roughly 'non X ≪pol Y', so the transcription's marginal '$X \underset{pol}{\ll} Y$' should carry the negation.
